userStories.title: P4C.3 residual — this-occurrence-vs-whole-series edit/delete UI wiring on /calendar
userStories.description: As a calendar user editing or deleting one occurrence of a recurring local event, I want an explicit 'this occurrence' versus 'whole series' choice so that my edit or delete applies exactly to the scope I intend, detached exceptions are preserved by whole-series changes, and no duplicate detached events appear on retries.
acceptanceCriteria: PLAN P4C.3 bullet (verbatim): daily/weekly/monthly, interval, weekdays, monthly position, count/until and skipped/detached occurrences. Explicit "this occurrence" versus "whole series" edit/delete. Stable series and occurrence IDs; no duplicate detached events on retries. Test DST, month-end/leap-year, locale week start, long ranges and timezone changes. Future-series split is not promised without an additional decision. — this story closes the last executor leg named in the ledger: the this-vs-series edit/delete UI wiring (browser proof stays orchestrator)

A scope-choice dialog (options: this occurrence / whole series — NO 'this and following' option; future-series split is explicitly not implemented) is shown when editing or deleting an event that carries recurrence series fields (seriesId/series state); plain non-recurring events edit and delete directly with no dialog

'This occurrence' edit routes through packages/twenty-front/src/modules/calendar/utils/applyCalendarEventEdit.ts scope 'this-occurrence' (materializes a detached replacement via detachCalendarOccurrence); repeated edits/retries of the same occurrence never create duplicate detached rows (engine idempotency, US-060..063)

'Whole series' edit uses scope 'whole-series' (rule swap, optional seriesStart) and already-detached occurrences/exclusions are preserved — unit-spec assert via the dispatcher's documented exception-preserving behavior

Delete mirrors the scopes via applyCalendarEventDelete.ts: occurrence → exclusion via skipCalendarOccurrence (re-delete idempotent, also drops that occurrence's detached replacement); whole series → anchor deletion with no leftover series state (dispatcher returns null)

Dialog reachable from the surfaces where local editing exists today (day view, agenda, event composer/details via useCalendarEventMutations.ts); week/month stay read-only exactly as shipped in US-052 — no new edit paths there

Do NOT touch packages/twenty-shared/src/utils/calendar-recurrence (verified engine), the server persistence slice, or recurrence fields/upgrade command 1789904000000; do NOT implement future-series split
Copy uses the Lingui t macro (fr+en source strings via macro; translation catalogs are NOT committed) and icons from twenty-ui/icon; light/dark via existing UI primitives

Unit specs cover: recurring vs non-recurring dialog decision, edit dispatch both scopes, delete dispatch both scopes incl. retry idempotency, exception preservation on whole-series edit, week/month no-dialog

userStories.title: P9.1 residual — directToolInvocation forced-tool arg threaded through sendChatMessage → ChatExecutionService (toolChoice)
userStories.description: As an assistant integration validating deterministic tool execution, I want an additive directToolInvocation argument on sendChatMessage that the server turns into a forced toolChoice for that turn so the Tier-2 live run can prove the named read-only tool executes deterministically, with fail-closed validation against the caller's tool catalog.
acceptanceCriteria: PLAN P9.1 assistant-surface ledger note (verbatim): Remains [~]: Tier-2 live dispatch + the recorded caveat — the server has no forced-tool parameter, so the live run must confirm the named tool executes deterministically, else thread a `directToolInvocation` arg through `sendChatMessage` → `ChatExecutionService` (`toolChoice`). — this story implements exactly that threading; the Tier-2 live dispatch stays orchestrator

Additive nullable directToolInvocation argument on the sendChatMessage mutation in packages/twenty-server/src/engine/metadata-modules/ai/ai-chat/resolvers/agent-chat.resolver.ts (minimal shape consistent with the existing @Args style; existing calls stay source-compatible)

Threaded into packages/twenty-server/src/engine/metadata-modules/ai/ai-chat/services/chat-execution.service.ts as a forced toolChoice for that turn — the service already has a toolChoice seam (~line 483, isWorkspaceSetupKickoffTurn ? 'required' : 'auto'); the kickoff-turn behavior is unchanged

Fail-closed validation: the named tool must resolve in the caller's catalog (ToolRegistryService.getCatalog(context) / getToolsByCategories — the P1.5-established native entry points); unknown, uninstalled-app, restricted-member or cross-workspace tool → refusal error with no provider call (mirrors US-064/065 semantics)
Mutating-category tools are never auto-executed: a forced invocation of a mutating tool still stages the PREFILL draft with requiresConfirmation per C6 — never posts/submits

Do NOT add any new AI registry/table/install hook (P1.5 law: reuse LogicFunctionToolProvider + toolTriggerSettings); do NOT change tool-provider surfaces; do NOT run graphql:generate (Tier 2 — the checked-in generated schema predates this arg; hand-written consumption is the prior-phase precedent); front-side composer wiring is deliberately out of scope (US-067 already verified composer invocation)

Unit specs: forced read-only tool executes deterministically (provider receives the forced choice); each denial case (unknown/uninstalled/restricted/foreign); mutating tool → draft not execution; no regression in the chat-execution suites incl. chat-execution.service.browsing-context.spec.ts

userStories.title: a2e-chat go-to-chat command/nav lands on /discussions instead of the chatChannels record index

userStories.title: WorkbenchWidgetDock StyledDockRoot invalid CSS fix — width transition and <1200px overlay media queries never fire
userStories.description: As a user of the workbench widgets dock, I want the dock's width CSS to be valid so that the width transition the reduced-motion accessibility rule targets actually fires and the <1200px floating-overlay media query actually applies.
acceptanceCriteria: Provenance (phase-10-report, verbatim): Pre-existing bug found, NOT fixed (out of scope): `WorkbenchWidgetDock.tsx` `StyledDockRoot` uses invalid CSS from its original commit (`min-workbenchwidgetdockwidth`, `workbenchwidgetdockwidth`, `@media (max-workbenchwidgetdockwidth: …)`), so the width transition the reduced-motion rule targets never fires and the <1200px overlay media queries never apply. Left untouched (layout change, not an a11y fix) — flagged for the orchestrator to schedule separately. PLAN P10 a11y tick note repeats: Pre-existing `StyledDockRoot` invalid-CSS bug (width transition / media queries never fire) flagged in phase-10-report for a separate layout fix

Replace the invalid property/media names in StyledDockRoot with valid CSS (custom-property-based widths consistent with the persisted localStorage keys a2e-widgets-*) so the width transition fires and the <1200px overlay media query applies

P2.4 semantics preserved — no functional change beyond the CSS fix: collapsible MINI/EXPANDED, resizable persisted widths, snap-collapse threshold (12px rule), floating overlay < 1200px, navigator float < 768px, pluggable widget registry
Additive only: no dock feature removed or renamed; reduced-motion rule now targets a transition that can actually fire (the a11y tick's goal)

Unit specs: the existing dock/tab suites stay green (11 suites / 85 tests per US-058); extend coverage as far as jsdom allows (assert the generated style uses var()-based widths and a px-based media query instead of the invalid names)
